lessons.title: Squares and square roots
lessons.summary: Use square facts and read exactly what the square-root sign and brackets mean.
lessons.objective: Use square facts and read exactly what the square-root sign and brackets mean.
lessons.before: Try the first small calculation without a calculator. Check it with the worked steps.
lessons.ideas:
Find the two equal sides and multiply them. Area is measured in square units.

Know the squares from 1 through 15 and recognise the same facts in reverse.

Read the grouping before you calculate.
lessons.method:
How do square areas help?

Arrange unit squares in equal rows and columns. A square with side 7 has seven rows of seven tiles.

How do I reverse a square?

Read the root sign as a request for the non-negative side length. Link it to a square fact you know.

What happens to a minus sign?

Put a finger under the base. A bracketed negative base is repeatedly multiplied with its sign. A minus outside the power is applied after the power.
mistakes: Doubling the side only finds two side lengths.
The standalone square-root sign does not ask for both signs.
A calculator must be told which terms the brackets contain.

examples.title: Find a square from its side
examples.question: A square banner is 6 cm wide. Work out its area in square centimetres.
examples.solution:
The height and width both equal 6 cm.

\(6^2=6\times6=36\).

The completed square covers 36 square centimetres.

examples.title: Read the positive square root
examples.question: Evaluate \(\sqrt{25}\).
examples.solution:
Find the non-negative number whose square is 25.

\(5\times5=25\) shows that 5 works.

Write 5. The square-root sign names the non-negative value.

examples.title: Read the base before squaring
examples.question: Evaluate \(-5^2\).
examples.solution:
The exponent belongs to the positive number. Apply the minus sign after squaring.

\(-(5\times 5)=-25\).

The signed value is \(-25\).

lessons.title: Cubes and cube roots
lessons.summary: Build a cube in layers and reverse its volume calculation.
lessons.objective: Build a cube in layers and reverse its volume calculation.
lessons.before: Try the first small calculation without a calculator. Check it with the worked steps.
lessons.ideas:
The volume in cubic units is the edge length cubed.

Remember the cubes of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 alongside their roots.

A negative number has exactly one real cube root.
lessons.method:
Why multiply three times?

Choose an edge length. Each flat square layer has that many rows and columns. Stack the same number of layers.

How do I recover an edge?

Look for the number that multiplies by itself twice to give a cube volume. The small 3 at the root sign means cube root.

Can a cube root be negative?

Two negative factors give a positive product. The third negative factor makes the product negative again.
mistakes: The square of the edge only counts one layer.
A square root would reverse two factors. Here there are three.
The small 3 belongs to the root sign. It does not multiply the root.

examples.title: Find the volume of a cube
examples.question: A cube has edge length 1 cm. Find its volume in cubic centimetres.
examples.solution:
One layer has \(1\times1=1\) unit cubes.

There are 1 layers. Multiply by 1 again.

The volume is \(1^3=1\) cubic centimetres.

examples.title: Recover an edge from the volume
examples.question: A model cube has volume 64 cubic centimetres. Find its edge length in centimetres.
examples.solution:
The edge appears three times in the volume calculation.

\(4\times4\times4=64\) proves that 4 works.

The cube root is \(\sqrt[3]{64}=4\). The edge is 4 cm.

examples.title: Read a negative cube root
examples.question: Evaluate \(\sqrt[3]{-64}\) exactly.
examples.solution:
A positive base cubed is positive. A negative base cubed is negative.

\((-4)\times(-4)\times(-4)=-64\) .

The only real cube root is \(-4\).

lessons.title: Other powers and roots
lessons.summary: Count copies of a base, then undo a fourth, fifth or sixth power.
lessons.objective: Count copies of a base, then undo a fourth, fifth or sixth power.
lessons.before: Try the first small calculation without a calculator. Check it with the worked steps.
lessons.ideas:
Say the repeated multiplication before using a calculator key.

Check your root by raising it to the power shown by the small index.

When the question says solve, check both signs and give all solutions.
lessons.method:
What do the small and large numbers mean?

The large number is the base. The small exponent tells you how many copies of the base to multiply.

What does the index on a root do?

Work backwards from the result. A fourth root asks for a base whose fourth power gives the number under the root sign. Similarly for other roots.

Does the equation ask for more than one number?

Compare the root symbol with an equation in an even power. Two opposite bases give the same positive even power.
mistakes: Swapping the base and exponent usually changes the result.
An even root of a positive number is written as the positive root. An odd root can be negative.
One correct value is incomplete if there is a second real solution.

examples.title: Evaluate a higher power
examples.question: Work out \(2^{4}\) without a calculator.
examples.solution:
The base is 2. The exponent 4 counts copies of the base.

Write \(2\times 2\times 2\times 2\). Multiply from left to right, one pair at a time.

\(2^{4}=16\).

examples.title: Undo a higher power
examples.question: Evaluate \(\sqrt[5]{-243}\) exactly.
examples.solution:
The small 5 tells you to reverse the 5th power.

Check \((-3)^{5}=-243\).

The value of the named root is \(-3\).

examples.title: Give both solutions
examples.question: Find all real numbers \(x\) satisfying \(x^{6}=4096\).
examples.solution:
\(4^{6}=4096\) gives one solution.

6 is even. Replacing the base by its negative leaves the same positive power.

The full answer is \(\{-4,4\}\). The root sign alone would give just 4.

lessons.title: Calculations with powers and roots
lessons.summary: Break a mixed calculation into smaller steps and check the grouping.
lessons.objective: Break a mixed calculation into smaller steps and check the grouping.
lessons.before: Try the first small calculation without a calculator. Check it with the worked steps.
lessons.ideas:
Work out the powers and roots, then finish the multiplication.

Treat a root's bar as grouping, like brackets around the quantity under it.

Raise both the numerator and the denominator to the stated power.
lessons.method:
Which pieces should I work out first?

Mark each complete power and each complete root before multiplying. Replace each piece by its value.

Where does the root bar end?

Read the whole expression before you calculate. A term to the right of the end of the bar belongs outside the root.

What if the base is a fraction?

Write the bracketed fraction twice for a square or three times for a cube. Then use ordinary fraction multiplication.
mistakes: A power or root can change the size by much more than its index suggests.
Do not include the next plus term unless the bar includes it.
If only the top changes, repeat the denominator too.

examples.title: Combine a power and a root
examples.question: Work out \(5^2\times\sqrt[3]{8}\) without a calculator.
examples.solution:
Calculate each power or root first.

The square is 25. The cube root is 2 because \(2^3=8\).

Multiply to give \(25\times2=50\).

examples.title: Check the reach of the root bar
examples.question: Work out \(\sqrt{16}+2^2\).
examples.solution:
Work out what the root sign covers. It stops before the plus sign.

The term under the root gives 4. The other term gives 4.

Add to get \(4+4=8\).

examples.title: Raise a fraction to a power
examples.question: Work out \(\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{2}\) exactly.
examples.solution:
The whole fraction is inside brackets. Use 2 copies.

Multiply the top numbers together, and the bottom numbers together.

The result is \(\frac{16}{25}\).

1. Work out \(\left(\frac{6}{5}\right)^{2}\) exactly.

    Show the method you used.

    [2]

  2. Work out \(10^2\times\sqrt[3]{27}\) without a calculator.

    Show the method you used.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The whole fraction is inside brackets. Use 2 copies.

Multiply the top numbers together, and the bottom numbers together.

The result is \(\frac{36}{25}\).

(b)

Calculate each power or root first.

The square is 100. The cube root is 3 because \(3^3=27\).

Multiply to give \(100\times3=300\).
questions.hint_html:
(a)

The brackets make the numerator and denominator part of the same base.

(b)

Treat each power or root as one number, then multiply.

marking_criteria.description_html: Multiply the top numbers together, and the bottom numbers together.
The square is 100. The cube root is 3 because \(3^3=27\).
